evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:412-415 — initializeAuth() (the mount-time effect) branch `if (storedUser && accessToken)` carries the comment 'Validate the token is not expired (basic check)' but then just calls setUser(storedUser). No expiry validation is performed: an expired access token persisted in localStorage is accepted verbatim and the app renders an authenticated session on cold boot.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx:221-233 — decodeJwtPayload() already extracts the unverified JWT claims (used by deriveActiveRole) and could read `exp`, so the guard the comment promises is trivially implementable with an existing utility; it is simply not wired into the cold-boot path.

Impact/reachability: on every reload with a stale token the user is treated as authenticated until the first API call returns 401 and the axios response interceptor (lib/api.ts:218-221) fires onUnauthorizedCallback. During that window protected UI can flash and deriveActiveRole runs against an expired token. Self-recovering via the 401 flow (hence medium, not high), but the comment/code mismatch is a real auth-correctness gap on the app's core session-init path.
